scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

The effectiveness of Yom Kippur depends on how individuals integrate its lessons into daily life. Thus, Yom Kippur can indeed change how seriously people take their mistakes, encouraging a more thoughtful and proactive stance in their lives.

First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a long day, and I can imagine how exhausting that must be. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. That seems like a good setup for maintaining a relationship without the constant stress of living together. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's 12 years old and really excited about it. Initially, I thought about asking my boyfriend to pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mom, she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. That's a bit confusing because he's been in my life for three years, and I would have thought he'd be more involved in my son's activities. So, I ended up paying for it myself, but to afford it, I had to extend my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. That's a significant increase in my workload. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could pick up and drop off my son on weekends because, obviously, I'm at work. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, while we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, whereas my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. He got really angry and told me that he has to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I'm not home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. He then suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him.
